deep.reconstruction:
Context: §§XXXVI–XL of E238 treat the buckling of a uniform cylindrical column of height a, flexural rigidity Ekk, total weight Q, carrying a top load P. The axis CMA is slightly bent. C is the loaded top, x = CP is measured down the axis and y = PM is the lateral deflection. The page derives the governing ODE and reduces it.

(1) Moment of the self-weight. On the previous page Euler holds M fixed and lets Y run along CM. The weight element (Q/a)dX at height X with deflection Y has lever arm (y−Y) about M. Integrating from 0 to x gives the moment (Q/a)(xy − ∫y dx). By integration by parts this equals (Q/a)∫_0^x X dY.

(2) Total bending moment at M: Py + (Q/a)∫x dy. With dx constant the radius of curvature is −dx²/ddy. The Bernoulli–Euler law (moment = Ekk/R) then gives Ekk·a·ddy + P a y dx² + Q dx² ∫x dy = 0. In modern form: EI y'' + P y + (Q/a)∫_0^x ξ y'(ξ) dξ = 0.

(3) Differentiating removes the integral: EI a y''' + (Pa + Qx) y' = 0. This is a second-order equation for the slope u = y', in effect a shear-force balance.

(4) Substitution s = 1 + Qx/(Pa), with ds constant and dx = Pa ds/Q. Writing dy = u ds, it gives (Q²EI/(P³a²)) u_ss + s u = 0. This is the Airy equation u'' + c s u = 0 with c = P³a²/(Q²EI).

(5) With u = exp∫v ds one obtains the Riccati equation dv + v² ds + c s ds = 0, i.e. v' + v² = −c s. This is the special Riccati equation v' + v² = A s^m with m = 1. That exponent is not among Daniel Bernoulli's integrable cases m = −4k/(2k±1) or m = −2. Euler therefore states that people have so far tried in vain to integrate it, and he abandons an exact solution.

On the next page he turns to a perturbative treatment for small Q/P.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. Checks: xy − ∫y dx = ∫x dy; the differentiation with dx constant; the change of variable to s, which gives the factor P³a³/Q² and so the coefficient Q²Ekk/(P³a²); and the Riccati reduction ddu = u(dv ds + v² ds²). All are correct.
Gap, not an error: the boundary conditions (∫x dy vanishing at x = 0, free and hinged ends, etc.) are not stated here. They are added on the next page, where 'en posant a = 0' should read x = 0.
'Tried in vain' is a heuristic claim, not a proof. Non-elementary integrability of this Riccati case was proved by Liouville in 1841.

ideas.what: Moment of the distributed self-weight about a section of a slightly bent column, computed via integration by parts as (Q/a)∫x dy
ideas.modern_name: Bending moment from axial distributed load (heavy column)
ideas.where_published: E238 (this paper); heavy-column theme revisited in E508 (1778)

ideas.what: Third-order ODE EI a y''' + (Pa + Qx) y' = 0 for a heavy column carrying a top load
ideas.modern_name: Buckling equation of a column under self-weight plus end load
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E238, then E508 for the pure self-weight case); later Greenhill 1881 (Bessel functions of order ±1/3)
ideas.where_published: E238; cf. E508 'De altitudine colonnarum sub proprio pondere corruentium'

ideas.what: Reduction of the slope equation to u'' + c s u = 0 by an affine change of variable
ideas.where_published: E238 (this page); Euler treats such equations via series elsewhere, e.g. E508

ideas.what: Logarithmic-derivative substitution u = exp∫v ds giving the special Riccati equation v' + v² + c s = 0, recognized as a non-integrable case
ideas.modern_name: Riccati transformation; special Riccati equation with exponent m = 1 (non-elementary, Liouville 1841)
ideas.where_published: Many Euler papers on the Riccati equation, e.g. E31, E70, E95, E284

missed.claim: Euler explicitly arrives at the Airy equation, in the guise of a Riccati equation with linear coefficient, as the governing equation for a heavy column with top load, about 80 years before Airy. Historians (e.g. Truesdell's Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies) do discuss this section, so it is probably not unknown. The point is rarely emphasised in histories of the Airy function, but it is a minor priority remark rather than a new result.
missed.quote: qui est un tel cas de l'équation de Riccati, qu'on s'est donné jusqu'ici en vain la peine de l'intégrer
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor historical note linking elastic stability to the prehistory of Airy and Bessel functions of order 1/3; no mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The derivation is correct and historically interesting: it is an early appearance of the Airy equation, in connection with the Riccati non-integrable case. However, the heavy-column problem in Euler is well documented (E238, E508; Truesdell). The reduction is standard, and Euler leaves the problem unsolved here.
transcription_corrections: Image reads 'a'outé' (broken print); the correct word is 'ajouté', as the transcription gives.
Use of long s (ſ) in the original is normalized in the transcription; no substantive discrepancies in the formulas were found.
